The test image shows a corn ear with whitish-gray fungal growth on and between kernels. This is a seed/ear disease. Top candidates from the seed/pod classes: Diplodia_Ear_Rot, Fusarium_Disease, Trichoderma_Ear_Rot, Gibberella_Disease, Aspergillus_Ear_Rot.

Let me view reference images one at a time, starting with one from each top candidate.
Fusarium reference shows whitish mold on scattered kernels - quite similar to the test image. Let me check Diplodia next.
Diplodia cross-section looks very different - mummified grayish-brown kernels. Let me check Trichoderma.
Trichoderma shows dark blue-green mold - doesn't match. Let me check Gibberella.
Gibberella shows pinkish-red mold starting at the tip - doesn't match the whitish scattered mold in the test image. Let me check Aspergillus.
Aspergillus shows olive-green powdery mold - doesn't match. Let me check Diplodia ear rot pod view and Common Smut seed.
Common Smut shows galls - completely different. The Fusarium reference was by far the closest match. Let me view one more Fusarium reference to confirm.

This second Fusarium reference is very similar to the test image: whitish to pinkish mold on scattered kernels across the ear, with some kernels appearing damaged and discolored, healthy yellow kernels interspersed. The pattern of whitish cottony/powdery fungal growth on individual kernels scattered across the ear matches closely.

Key observations:
- Test image: whitish-gray mold on and between kernels, scattered across the ear (not concentrated at tip or base)
- Fusarium references: very similar whitish to pinkish mold scattered on kernels
- Not Gibberella (pink mold at tip), not Aspergillus (olive-green), not Trichoderma (dark blue-green), not Diplodia (white mycelium from base, mummified), not Common Smut (galls)
